about.description:
Harmonica is a Python library for processing and modeling gravity and
magnetic data. It includes common processing steps, like calculation of
Bouguer and terrain corrections, reduction to the pole, upward
continuation, equivalent layers, and more. There are forward modeling
functions for basic geometric shapes, like spheres, prisms, polygonal
prisms, and tesseroids. The inversion methods are implemented as classes
with an interface inspired by scikit-learn (like Verde).
about.summary: Forward modeling, inversion, and processing gravity and magnetic data

raw_meta_yaml:
schema_version: 1

context:
  version: "0.7.0"

package:
  name: harmonica
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  url: https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/source/h/harmonica/harmonica-${{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: a4f889b121778479a87d94e481c423e51dd4355593fbab497ad357c0c7fa219a

build:
  number: 2
  noarch: python
  script: ${{ PYTHON }} -m pip install . -vv

requirements:
  host:
    - python ${{ python_min }}.*
    - setuptools >=61
    - setuptools-scm >=8.0.3
    - pip
  run:
    - python >=${{ python_min }}
    - numpy >=1.23
    - pandas >=1.4
    - scipy >=1.9
    - scikit-learn >=1.0
    - numba >=0.53
    - xarray >=2022.03
    - verde >=1.8.1
    - xrft >=1.0
    - choclo >=0.1

tests:
  - python:
      imports:
        - harmonica
      pip_check: true
      python_version:
        - ${{ python_min }}.*
        - "*"
  - requirements:
      run:
        - python ${{ python_min }}.*
    script:
      - python -c "import harmonica; assert harmonica.__version__ != '0.0.0'"

about:
  summary: Forward modeling, inversion, and processing gravity and magnetic data
  license: BSD-3-Clause
  license_file: LICENSE.txt
  homepage: https://pypi.org/project/harmonica/
  documentation: https://www.fatiando.org/harmonica
  repository: https://github.com/fatiando/harmonica
  description: |
    Harmonica is a Python library for processing and modeling gravity and
    magnetic data. It includes common processing steps, like calculation of
    Bouguer and terrain corrections, reduction to the pole, upward
    continuation, equivalent layers, and more. There are forward modeling
    functions for basic geometric shapes, like spheres, prisms, polygonal
    prisms, and tesseroids. The inversion methods are implemented as classes
    with an interface inspired by scikit-learn (like Verde).

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - mdtanker
    - leouieda
    - santisoler
